Subject: SLO runbook & cost levers — Nimbus Health discovery follow-up

Hi Marian / CloudOps,

Thanks again for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can narrow pilot scope: 

Summary of your SLO targets (call notes):
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn clinical-assist prompts (~512 tokens); p50 <= 120ms.
- Throughput: sustained 250 reqs/min during business hours, spiky bursts to 800 reqs/min for campaign windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent streams 8–12, peak concurrency target 36.
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for the assistant UI (low startup latency).

Primary constraints: PHI-sensitive data (on-prem VPC first), and tight latency targets for the in-clinic assistant.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
1) We'll run a focused perf qualification: 72-hour pilot in your staging VPC to exercise 3 representative prompts (clinical summary, triage, coding assist).
2) Action: please share a short suite of 6–10 prompt examples and the expected token lengths (or we can use the samples you uploaded).
3) We will provide a runbook with cost/perf levers and an expected cost range (baseline + optimized).
4) Tentative owners: Redwood SE (Sean) will run the load tests; Vivek will coordinate quantization profiles and model variants; Ava will own the commercial proposal.

Attachment: I attached an initial SLO matrix with assumptions we discussed. [attachment: slo_matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

A few initial notes on levers so you have context before our qualification run:
- Continuous batching: valuable at steady throughput to reduce per-token overhead, but must be tuned carefully for streaming to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- KV/prefix caching: for episodic prompts (patient context), caching will reduce model work for repeated prefixes and improve tail latency.
- Quantization profiles: 4-bit q4_0 and mixed-precision for some model families can cut inference compute ~2–3x with modest quality loss; we’ll evaluate on your prompts.
- Model variants: propose evaluating a latency-optimized distilled variant for in-clinic fast-path and a higher-quality base variant for overnight batch jobs.

Proposed dates: pilot kickoff on Mon 2026-10-26; load window Wed/Thu; results and cost runbook by Fri 2026-10-30.

Please reply with prompt samples and any mandatory security checklist items we should know about before VPC access.

Thanks,

Marian — quick technical recap and a first-pass cost/latency sketch based on the 8 prompts you dropped. Details in the attached perf profile PDF. [attachment: redwood_perf_profile.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]

Key assumptions used for estimates:
- Model family: LlamaX-13B equivalent; baseline float16, opt-quant q4_0 and a distilled 7B fast variant for latency path.
- Sequence: avg request 512 tokens; streaming enabled for first 64 tokens to hit interactive feel.
- HW: A100-class for baseline; T4 for cheapest quantized path in Dedicated pockets.

Preliminary numbers (ballpark):
- Baseline (no quant): p95 ~ 300ms per prompt on A100 at 1 concurrent stream; cost ~= $0.010 per prompt.
- Quantized + batching (q4_0, continuous batching tuned): p95 ~ 180–230ms; cost ~= $0.004–$0.006 per prompt.
- Distilled 7B variant (latency path): p95 ~ 90–130ms; cost ~= $0.002–$0.003 per prompt.

Trade-offs and recommended runbook steps: 
1) Hybrid routing: route critical UI prompts to the distilled 7B under an A/B policy; route other requests to quantized 13B with prefix caching. This hits the 80–120ms streaming requirement for first-byte while keeping quality high for complex cases.
2) Streaming + batching config: use micro-batches with max_hold_ms = 12 and token-based batching threshold to avoid adding >40ms headroom to first-byte. We'll test these in the pilot.
3) KV/prefix caching: results show up to 40% token reduction for repeated patient-context prompts on our sample — big win for tail latency.
4) Autoscaling buffers: reserve burst slots (Dedicated capacity) to handle 3x baseline peaks; Redwood Dedicated can pre-warm pools for clinical hours.

Open items we need from Nimbus:
- Representative latency probe (a single TCP ping + 1 warm request) from your clinic VM to our staging endpoint.
- Confirmation which 2 prompts must always go to the latency path vs. candidate pool.

I’ll schedule the first load window for Wed 10/28 02:00–06:00 PT unless you prefer a different window.
